description: Everyone can visit the Brandenburg Gate and Museum Island! This tour takes you through a part of Berlin-Mitte that many don't know yet. Even though it has an extremely exciting history. We meet at Hackescher Markt and explore the old Jewish Berlin there. Where did the largest spontaneous protest against the Holocaust take place? Where did a brave Berliner hide blind Jews from the Nazis? And what happened to Berlin's oldest Jewish cemetery? Impressive monuments, incredible stories and magical backyards can be discovered here. We see one of the only places where the wild, creative and colorful charm of the 90s can still be seen. I will also show you my favorite street in all of Berlin - the Grosse Hamburger street - because there are so many stories to tell and time seems to have stopped here. How was the new synagogue saved? And why did Martin Luther King come to East Berlin? Then we travel by subway to the oldest part of the city, which is completely off the radar for most people. Here we learn what the Underground Station Klosterstraße has in common with old Babylon. Where does Berlin's medieval city wall still stand? In which restaurant is Napoleon supposed to have dined? And where was the world's first museum against war? From the ruins of Berlin‘s old monastery we walk to the Spree river.
locationDescription: We meet at Hackescher Markt and from there we go to the Rosenstrasse monument and on to the Grosse Hamburger Strasse. Here is the oldest Jewish cemetery in Berlin and the Sophienkirche. The New Synagogue is around the corner. From Sophienstrasse we go into the Schwarzenberg house to the Otto Weidt Museum. Then by underground to Klosterstraße and along the city wall, parochial church, old and new town house to the Spree River
